text:
incident-bot: PAGER: High-sev alert for tenant acmecorp in Dedicated Pool 'eu-west-1-ded-42' — sudden drop in quality metrics after quantization profile vQ3 rollout. Affected API: /v1/generate (model: redwood/openlm-redsuite-v2:q:vQ3). Error: quality-regression-delta > 0.25 ROUGE-L. Paging oncall-ml. Please ACK and triage. :rotating_light:

oncall-ml: ACKing. I'm up. Quick checks: is this limited to acmecorp dedicated pool or global?

jordan: looking now — initial logs show 100% of requests for tenant acmecorp routed to quant profile vQ3 since 2026-03-15T02:12Z (scheduled rollout). Other tenants on same pool still on vQ2. Running quick eval against our regression set for acmecorp prompts.

jordan: sample diff from a few requests (expected vs observed):
```
EXPECTED: "Summary: The release clarifies the billing window and improves idempotency handling."
OBSERVED: "Summary: Billing window is broken. Idempotency unknown."
```

jordan: BLEU/ROUGE drop confirmed locally — matches alert. Looks isolated to the quantized model variant.

lee: assigning mitigation priorities: 1) immediate customer-visible rollback or routing to fallback 2) preserve tenant isolation (no cross-tenant cache bleed) 3) postmortem + revert plan.

lee: propose immediate temporary routing to hosted non-quantized model for acmecorp while we investigate. Command to create routing rule: 
```bash
redwood routes create --tenant acmecorp --match "pool:eu-west-1-ded-42" --route-to "model:redwood/openlm-redsuite-v2:unquantized:v2.13" --priority 1000 --ttl 3600
```

oncall-ml: I'll run the route and then invalidate KV prefix cache for that tenant.

oncall-ml: running: 
```bash
# apply routing
$ redwood routes create --tenant acmecorp --match "pool:eu-west-1-ded-42" --route-to "model:redwood/openlm-redsuite-v2:unquantized:v2.13" --priority 1000 --ttl 3600
Applied route id=rt_0a1b2c3d status=active
# invalidate KV cache
$ redwood cache invalidate --tenant acmecorp --prefix kv:openlm-redsuite
Invalidation queued (job id=job_9922)
```

oncall-ml: route applied and cache invalidation queued. Monitoring request samples now.

jordan: I pulled post-route samples — output quality returned to baseline on ~95% of recent calls. Good. Logging still shows some concurrent requests hitting the quantized binary for a short window (in-flight), but rollback will converge.

amy_acct: I pinged Acme support contact (Mark) at 02:25Z — told them we're rolling them to a non-quantized model and will follow up on root cause. They've asked for ETA and whether there was data exposure. 

maria_cs: are we sure tenant isolation was preserved? acmecorp is in a VPC/dedicated pool so extra care. I need confirmation no other tenants saw degraded quality.

sre-oncall: verified via routing logs and metrics — only acmecorp shows drop. No cross-tenant routing changes. KV cache keys are namespaced by tenant; invalidation scoped to acmecorp. No evidence of data bleed. Will attach correlation graphs in postmortem.

lee: next actions: 1) keep acmecorp on fallback unquantized model for now, 2) roll back vQ3 quantization profile from dedicated pool staging, 3) run full regression/eval suite against acmecorp promptset and broader smoke tests, 4) create canary gating for future quant profile rollouts into dedicated pools. I'm documenting steps here.

lee: rollback command (will patch quant profiles on the dedicated pool):
```bash
# rollback quant profile vQ3 from pool
$ redwood pool update --pool eu-west-1-ded-42 --quant-profile "default:vQ2" --dry-run=false 
POOL_UPDATE: started job=pool_update_5589
```

oncall-ml: started rollback at 02:34Z. Job status: pool_update_5589 -> in_progress. I'll monitor, and if anything blocks, I'll escalate to eng-runtime.

jordan: while that runs, saved a few failing examples and pushed to the regression bucket at s3://redwood-regressions/acmecorp/2026-03-15/. Also triggered nightly eval for acmecorp prompts.

amy_acct: customer requested a call — scheduled a quick bridge at 03:00Z to confirm mitigation and next steps. Will join and hand off notes.

maria_cs: please confirm we won't reapply vQ3 automatically. Is there an automated rollout job that will retry?

lee: good catch — there is an automated quant-rollout pipeline for pools. I paused the pipeline for eu-west-1-ded-42 and set a manual approval gate. Command: 
```bash
redwood rollout pause --pool eu-west-1-ded-42 --pipeline quant-rollout-main
```
Response: pipeline quant-rollout-main paused for pool eu-west-1-ded-42 (by lee).

sre-oncall: pool_update_5589 completed at 02:40Z. All nodes now report quant-profile default:vQ2. No errors.

oncall-ml: confirming post-rollback eval: ROUGE/L/BLEU back to baseline on sampled set. Good.

oncall-ml: I'm handing off monitoring + postmortem to lee — my shift ends in 20m. Lee, can you pick up and lead the follow-ups? Key items: add regression test for tenant-specific quant changes, update deployment playbook with canary gating, notify infra that quant profile rollout must have tenant-scoped safety nets.

lee: taking over. I'll own the postmortem + action items. Adding follow-ups to the incident board and assigning owners.

lee: postmortem next steps (short):
- Action (oncall-ml): add targeted regression tests and integrate into quant-rollout gating.
- Action (eng-runtime): implement tenant-scoped canary limits (no global auto-apply to dedicated pools).
- Action (sre): add metric alerting for per-tenant quality deltas with stricter thresholds for dedicated pools.
- Action (acct/cs): follow up with acmecorp with RCA and remediation plan; offer extended monitoring.

amy_acct: I'll own the customer communication and the scheduled 03:00Z call. Will share notes & next steps on the account thread after the call.

maria_cs: file created: INC-2026-ACME-QUANT-REG (internal), linking evidence and samples.

lee: marking this thread as mitigated. If any new regressions appear, re-open page. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident state updated -> mitigated by oncall-ml, assigned to lee for postmortem. Closed by system at 03:12Z.
